proof_attempt_summary: The run attempted a same-class attainable minimax frontier for sharp binary-IV ATE endpoints. It proved exact measurable dual attainment, a base-preserving envelope/regularity criterion, finite-sample known-propensity outer coverage, oracle/eventwise composition, and compatible contact lower bounds, then repaired every math-referee defect to a final PASS. The attainable root-n theorem was honestly retracted because no training-computable learner/optimizer and matching fixed-P0 upper theory were constructed; those questions remain open and cap the result at incremental tier.
tldr: The note proves jointly measurable exact dual attainment for sharp bounded-outcome binary-IV average treatment effect sets, a base-preserving envelope for population endpoint functionals, and a projected-score regularity criterion. With known instrument propensities, held-out intervals have finite-sample outer coverage for arbitrary evaluated exact-feasible candidates. A baseline-class first-order oracle comparison bounds finite-sieve dual regret. The proved eventwise composition bounds outward excess on the intersection of externally specified pilot, oracle-optimization, and held-out concentration events; no class-uniform probability or rate achievability is proved. Separately, an atomic submodel yields a fixed-smoothness polynomial lower bound on \(\mathcal P_0\), and a specified full-baseline experiment is not uniformly consistent. Attainable root-\(n_e\) behavior and matching same-class rates remain open.
